---
title: "Research Workflows"
---

The `pro` profile extends a workload with controlled systems conditions while
preserving its identity and quality target. It is intended for bounded,
single-node studies. One run is enough to test the workflow and evaluate the
quality contract, but it is not stability or publication evidence.

## Start With a Research Question

Use a versioned experiment plan when the study has more than one condition.
The plan records the hypothesis, controlled settings, device policy, output
location, and role of each condition.

```bash
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml
```

The dry run is the review point. Confirm the workload, dataset, mode, phase,
device, baseline, candidate, and output location before any expensive work.

## Compare Compatible Conditions

A plan may label one condition as `baseline` and another as `candidate`. The
dashboard shows a descriptive throughput delta only when their comparison
fingerprints are compatible. Quality uses normalized target attainment, where
100% means the declared gate was reached. Unrelated raw metrics never share an
axis.

The included plan changes image-classification batch size while holding the
quality contract fixed. It is a small example of the full research loop.

1. State the systems hypothesis.
2. Change one declared independent variable.
3. Keep the evaluation set, quality target, checkpoint lineage, and device
   policy controlled.
4. Inspect each condition before reading the delta.
5. Preserve the plan, aggregate report, child reports, and manifests together.

## Interpret One-Run Evidence

A completed `pro` run can establish that the study design executes, the
declared quality contract was evaluated, and the observed result belongs to the
recorded configuration. It cannot establish a stable distribution or a
publication-ready performance claim. Repetition, uncertainty analysis,
independent reproduction, and release review belong to the later stability and
production phases.

## Preflight Expensive Work

Inspect the selected workload and assets before running it.

```bash
uv run mlperf show WORKLOAD
uv run mlperf doctor --workload WORKLOAD --profile pro
uv run mlperf fetch --workload WORKLOAD --profile pro --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --workload WORKLOAD --profile pro --dry-run
```

There is no general `run --resume` option yet. Long-running studies should use
an explicit output directory and follow the recovery boundary documented on the
workload page. MiniGo remains a local-execution blocker, so its page leads
with preflight and handoff instructions rather than a generic laptop run.

## Preserve the Review Packet

Keep the following files together for a co-author or artifact reviewer.

- The exact experiment-plan YAML and its recorded SHA-256
- The aggregate JSON, HTML, and CSV reports
- Every condition report and `.provd.json` manifest
- The dataset and model dossiers recorded in each report
- A short interpretation that distinguishes execution, quality, comparison,
  and repeatability claims

Use the [results guide](results.qmd) to interpret the dashboard and the
[readiness page](../readiness.qmd) to see current workload limitations.
